title: Cultural & Typographic Evaluation Kit
summary: How can evaluators separate factual cultural/typographic constraint failures from subjective aesthetic preference, while documenting disagreement and source provenance?
evidence_level: Measured check self-consistency and adversarial robustness on template artifacts; no model or rater results
contribution: Concept, design criteria, typographic research and editorial: ilghar.studio.
architecture: Separate factual and aesthetic rubric axes
Versioned evaluation report and design examples

results.metric: automated check detection of generated corruptions
false positives on clean template artifacts

limitations: No generative model outputs evaluated yet; artifacts are templates and hand-written examples.
No real human annotations; aesthetic axes are unmeasured. Synthetic annotations are labelled synthetic.
C03/C04 are human-review-only; text checks cannot see font shaping or rendering.
Grid and keyboard checks work on declared numbers and text, never on screenshots.
Illustrations are editorial images only; the native diagram is authoritative.
pitch: A kit for judging generated design work the way a typographer would: first the facts you can check (the right Persian letters, the right reading order, the grid that actually adds up), then taste, kept separate and allowed to disagree.
problem: Image and layout generators produce posters, cards and keyboards that look plausible and are quietly wrong. Persian keycaps with the same letter printed four times. An Arabic kāf where Persian needs keheh. A missing zero-width non-joiner that breaks a word in two. A template whose inside margin is 37.89 pt while every other margin is 36. A literary or cultural object dropped in as decoration, with no reason to be there.

Most evaluations fold all of this into one “quality” score, so a factual error and a matter of taste end up on the same scale, and the people who notice the error are outvoted by the people who liked the colours.

This kit keeps the two apart. Factual constraints are checked by deterministic code at the level of Unicode code points and arithmetic. Aesthetic judgements are collected from raters as distributions, never averaged into a verdict, and disagreement is flagged for adjudication. Rater identity is never used as evidence of expertise: an annotation that carries a nationality field is rejected.

audience.who: Teams evaluating image, layout or type generators
audience.why: Code-point-exact checks for Persian and mixed-direction text, and a clear line between “wrong” and “I don’t like it”.
A grid checker that tells you whether margins, gutters and baseline really form the square, rhythmic module you asked for.
Annotation schemas that preserve minority opinions and uncertainty, and refuse identity-based shortcuts.

how.title: Cleared brief + constraints
how.body: Each case states what must be true (exact title glyphs, reading order, required fields, diagram stages) and records rights and review status for every reference.

how.title: Candidate artifact
how.body: Original or licensed examples only. The M04 slice renders a right-to-left SVG card from a spec, with native text, never text baked into pixels.

how.title: Factual checks
how.body: glyph_exact, reading_order, required_fields and diagram_fidelity return pass, fail or uncertain with evidence. Anything that needs eyes is marked human-review, never guessed.

how.title: Taste, separately
how.body: Aesthetic axes such as hierarchy are collected as rating distributions with n, not merged into the factual verdict.

how.title: Disagreement and adjudication
how.body: Conflicting rater verdicts are flagged needs_adjudication. Malformed or identity-bearing annotations are rejected with reasons.

how.title: Grid and keyboard checks
how.body: New: grid verifies margins, gutters, square modules and baseline rhythm by arithmetic; keyboard checks Persian keycaps for duplicates, look-alikes and missing letters.

hero.alt: A plum typewriter with blank keycaps above a square modular grid sheet, a brass line gauge and a loupe.
hero.caption: Blank keys on purpose: letters belong in native text that can be checked, not in pixels. Editorial illustration.

figures.alt: Two trays divided by a plum ruler: measuring tools on the left, swatches and a dried flower on the right.
figures.caption: Facts on one side, taste on the other, and a ruler between them.

commands.what: Vertical slice: render RTL SVG cards from specs and run the checks on them. Cases without an automatable spec stay empty rather than pass.
Validate the case collection and list which constraints per case can be checked by code.
Corruption suite: inject known errors (Arabic kāf/yeh, dropped ZWNJ, swapped order, invented metric) and measure detection.
Adversarial suite for checks and aggregation (bidi controls, Persian digits, percent signs, malformed annotations).
New. The recorded A4 template: 6×9 grid, 12 pt gutter, margins declared equal but inside set to 37.89 pt.

schemas.what: One case: id, kind, brief, required_text, constraints, aesthetic_axes, rights, review_status, gold_verdict (null until reviewed).
One rater’s annotation: case_id, artifact_id, rater_id, constraint_results, aesthetic_ratings, notes. No identity fields allowed.
